data.turoyo: Qrele lu dewo l ḥayye, ṣfəllela. Nafəq ḥayye smiṯo
data.translation: Dort rief der Wolf einer Schlange, indem er ihr pfiff; in Folge dessen kam eine blinde Schlange hervor.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; addressee suffix or l-NP, without deriving a new summoning sense.

data.turoyo: Ṣfəlle l ḥreto, nafəq ḥḏo, ḥaša, ṣliḥo.
data.translation: Dann pfiff er einer andern; es kam eine hervor mit gespaltenem Rücken.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; addressee suffix or l-NP, without deriving a new summoning sense.

data.turoyo: Ṣfəlle l ḥreto, nafəq ḥḏo qarʕa kibe xəd qaṭuno, pərč b qarʕa hawi ṣiṭo.
data.translation: Dann pfiff er einer dritten; da kam eine Schlange hervor mit einem Kopfe gleich dem einer Katze; das Haar auf demselben war spannenlang.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; addressee suffix or l-NP, without deriving a new summoning sense.

summary: Three clear I Preterit attestations match ṣfəlle and the inherited pfeifen gloss, with overt actor/recipient suffix distinction in ṣfəllela.

The JTM candidate has uncertain root and stem. A collision event in the translation is insufficient to publish a homonymous root or new II stem without a secure reading; no unattested base form is reconstructed.
The three snake episodes are parallel in function, but provide full textual contexts and both suffixed and nominal addressees for a cell previously containing only an isolated grammar form.
Check JTM 5.3/8 kməṣforət against the edition or recording: exact consonants, vowels, root and whether the meaning is collision or another action. A separate homonym or II stem remains unestablished.
Whistling can be directed to an addressee through -la or an l-NP; a snake responding does not lexicalize summon as a distinct meaning.
